rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable insect bites (localised itchy rash)
rule_level_problems.problem: Evidence (Pruritic rash + red papule) is a subset of the scabies picture (severe itching + red papule + burrows), and the task anchor makes Pruritic rash likely to be recorded. Every scabies patient will also get 'Insect bites probable'. On the page, scabies is a separate pre-flowchart exit (-> 84), not a Yes-branch case. No (no Burrows in skin) or similar exclusion is present.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable tinea corporis (localised itchy rash)
rule_level_problems.problem: A bare 'or' of single findings with no presenting-complaint anchor, no site gate (head/face/trunk/limbs) and no central clearing. 'Scaly skin + Annular shape' alone gives probable tinea corporis, including on the feet, where it co-fires with tinea pedis, and for an annular scaly herald patch.

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable pityriasis rosea (localised itchy rash)
rule_level_problems.problem: Scale is dropped from both the herald patch (fine scale in centre) and the secondary oval patches, and the herald-then-eruption sequence (within 2 weeks) is lost. The rule rests on a large annular lesion on chest/back plus multiple small oval lesions.

The exclusivity of the 'red itchy bumps' Yes branch versus the 'No: check site' branch is not represented. Psoriasis, pityriasis rosea and the tinea rules can co-fire with insect bites, papular urticaria and impetigo. Lower impact because the evidence sets mostly differ.

Pruritic rash is in the evidence for eczema, insect bites, papular urticaria and impetigo, but not for scabies, FDE, psoriasis, pityriasis rosea or the tinea rules, so those fire without the presenting complaint. Pruritic rash is also not a recorded common symptom or warning sign, so the check_for task may never trigger. This needs a note in remaining-questions.

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for localised itchy rash conditions
rule_level_problems.problem: The page says 'check nails' and offers pitted nails for psoriasis, but nails are not in check_for (Pitting of nails (disorder) exists). Otherwise every check_for item is consumed by a rule, and every probable-rule evidence item is in the check_for or the task due_to.

summary: Every 'likely' on the page has a probable rule with a valid SNOMED concept (all 54 concepts exist), and the scabies, eczema, FDE, insect-bite family, psoriasis and tinea pedis criteria are faithful. The most consequential problems are over-firing. The insect bites rule fires for every scabies patient. Tinea corporis fires on any annular scaly finding, with no central clearing and no site gate. Pityriasis rosea has lost the scale and the herald-then-eruption sequence that distinguish it. The red box is only a cross-reference to page 82, so correctly no priority evaluation.
